text: basic and good value. It is at the side of the square housing the main bus station and the railway station. It is the terminus for the No.16 bus which serves the Airport ( at the Airport). the historic Medina is about a DRH 10 (EUR 1 00) ride away in a "Petit Taxi". The grounds were well kept and there is an arrow shaped swimming pool about 15 metres long. It is unheated and I could not swim for more than 15 minutes without feeling distinctly chilly. The rooms on the side facing the garden will be quieter than those facing the bus station, The breakfasts in the hotel were poor the markets overflowing with a wide variety of fruits) and what seemed to be factory-made baguettes ( the markets having an abundance of breads of many types). The three nights including breakfast cost less than GBP 100 (EUR 150) so it was good value. The location is very close to train station. text: This hotel is great for a short stay in Marrakech the rooms are spacious enough and the beds are very comfortable. The staff are exceptionally friendly and helpful one of the warmest welcomes you could wish for! There is the option to have your breakfast al fresco as there are many seats outside and around the pool. The breakfast buffet I would definately reccomend having breakfast in Jama el Fna on one of the nearby busier streets. The location is ideal for the Marrakech Centre Gare train station and is also right next to the Supratours Bus Station where you can catch a bus to the likes of Essaouira, Casablanca It's especially convenient for going to and from Jama el fna in a way which helps avoiding rip off taxi's. It tours the whole city and even ventures out to the leafy outskirts where you get great views of the mountains.There is a stop 50 yards from the Ibis Hotel. The hotel is situated on the main road next to the railway station about 3 maybe 4 km away from the centre of the city. We had an adequate twin room overlooking the hotel garden and station. The rooms are basically decorated with enough storage (just) for the five nights we were staying. The beds are reasonable and the bathroom has all you need with a fairly powerful and spacious shower (no bath). the decor is a bit tired the carpet a bit threadbare and the lighting not great. Housekeeping is a bit hit and miss, they do respect the "do not disturb" signs. The towels which are rationed to one basic bath towel per person are paper-thin This entitled us to a choice of salad soup (vegetable every day) to start The à la carte menu seems reasonably priced so probably best to skip the prepaid deal Service at the hotel was fairly inconsistent one man on reception was particularly helpful so when we needed towels (as they were not provided twice) the security guard had to get them for us.The reception sseemed understaffed when coach parties arrived. One of the waiters (head waiter?) On our last night it seemed that the regular waiting staff were (there were only two) both off All in all okay for a two night stay I guess any longer and you'd be best to upgrade to a better hotel. The hotel seems to be a travellers inn rather than a base for a weeks holiday.
